summary.text: Republican Caroleene Dobson won the November 3, 2026 election for Alabama secretary of state, defeating Wayne Rogers, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
She is a Montgomery attorney who was the 2024 Republican nominee in Alabama's 2nd Congressional District.

paragraphs.text: Dobson was born and raised on her family's farm in Monroe County. She holds an undergraduate degree from Harvard College and a law degree from Baylor University School of Law.
She is a shareholder at the Maynard Nexsen law firm in Montgomery, where she focuses on natural resources, commercial finance and real estate law.
Dobson won the Republican nomination in Alabama's 2nd Congressional District in 2024 and lost to Democratic Rep. Shomari Figures in the general election, with 45% of the vote.
Her campaign centered on election-law enforcement and lower business fees.
Caroleene Dobson won the November 3, 2026 general election for secretary of state with 54.6% of the vote to Wayne Rogers's 45.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
